messages:
Jordan (Support): Heads up — we've got three customers this morning reporting regressions after last night's model rollout. They say the assistant is returning previously-seen, out-of-date completion snippets mixed into new responses. Looks like context is being mangled, not a model hallucination.

Anna (Eng-SRE): Which rollout ID / commit? Any shared pattern across tenants?

Jordan (Support): Rollout r2025-03-01-14: commit 9f3a2b. Affected customers are: AcmePay (prod), DataBeacon (staging->prod), and Tutorly (prod). All on hosted-api region us-west-2. They attached transcripts where a previous answer about pricing shows up inside unrelated prompts.

Sam (Eng-ML): Can you paste a short repro transcript? Specifically the assistant output that looks stale.

Jordan (Support): Sure, from AcmePay: 
```
User: "How do I set up webhooks?"
Assistant: "...you can configure webhooks in Settings > Integrations. Also, your session key: 0x9a... (from old conversation about API keys)"
```
So the assistant injects the old API-key-like snippet. Not just repetition — it's mixing prefixes.

Priya (Eng-Platform): That screams KV/prefix cache bleed. We recently changed the model packaging for r2025-03-01: we swapped the runtime to use shared prefix caching across model family for perf. Looks like we forgot to namespace by rollout id/model-sha.

DeployBot: deploy r2025-03-01-14 started at 2025-03-01T14:07Z, finished 2025-03-01T14:12Z. Canary passed.

Anna (Eng-SRE): Ok, immediate triage: 1) stop routing new traffic to the rollout 2) invalidate KV/prefix caches for affected model family 3) run targeted replay to confirm. Sam/Priya can you confirm invalidation API and keys we should hit?

Sam (Eng-ML): Invalidation endpoint exists but it's gated. For now we can call internal /internal/cache/invalidate with a prefix. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood.local/internal/cache/invalidate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prefix": "model:openqa:family-v2:"}'
```
That will evict keys starting with that prefix across the memcached/redis cluster. But caution: if the root cause is mismatched key format (old keys still valid for new model), invalidation will clear the stale entries.

Jordan (Support): Can we flush only customer scopes rather than global? AcmePay is sensitive to downtime.

Priya (Eng-Platform): We can target tenant-scoped prefixes, e.g. "model:openqa:family-v2:tenant:acmepay:". I'll run invalidations per-tenant first. Also creating a short TTL bump to avoid immediate reappearance while we patch.

Anna (Eng-SRE): I'm going to pivot traffic to previous stable rollout r2025-02-27-09 for impacted customers. Doing canary redirect now. OncallBot, show me the status.

OncallBot: Traffic shift triggered. 3 tenants routed to r2025-02-27-09. Expected convergence 60s.

Sam (Eng-ML): We should also inspect logs for cache hits where model_version != model_namespace stored in key metadata. Searching logs for kv.get with prefix 'model:openqa:family-v2:' and comparing stored header. Example log excerpt: 
```
[2025-03-02T02:21:11Z] kv.get key=model:openqa:family-v2:session:abc123 hit=true stored_meta={model_sha: 4d7b2, rollout: r2025-02-10-11}
[2025-03-02T02:21:11Z] runtime.resolve model=9f3a2b applied_cached_kv=true
```
That shows the new runtime loading a cached KV produced by an older runtime.

Jordan (Support): Customers are asking for timeline and rollback confirmation. I told AcmePay we have engineers looking and may do targeted cache clear.

Priya (Eng-Platform): I'll run per-tenant invalidations for AcmePay and Tutorly now, and set TTL 30s on the model family prefix to prevent reuse: 
```
# invalidate and set short TTL
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood.local/internal/cache/invalidate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"prefix":"model:openqa:family-v2:tenant:acmepay:", "ttl":30}'
```
Then monitor reproductions.

Anna (Eng-SRE): After traffic switch and cache invalidation, I'm seeing reduced error reports. Can we add an automated guard in the rollout pipeline to bump the cache namespace whenever model packaging changes? That would avoid manual clears.

Sam (Eng-ML): Agreed. Short-term patch: ensure runtime attaches namespace header 'model_namespace' that includes model_sha+rollout. We'll roll that change and include a migration that renames existing keys (rekey) for safe handover. Long-term: orchestration should always create a unique cache prefix per deployment.

Jordan (Support): Customer comms: I'm telling AcmePay we rolled back traffic and are invalidating tenant caches; expected fix within 10-15 minutes. Will loop back with transcript when verified. They appreciate the quick mitigation. :thumbsup: 

Priya (Eng-Platform): Done with targeted invalidation for acmepay and tutorly. TTL set. Monitoring logs now.

OncallBot: All clear for acmepay: recent requests show no stale snippets in the last 12 minutes.

Sam (Eng-ML): I'll open a follow-up PR to change cache namespace behavior and add integration test covering cross-rollout cache collisions. Also adding a rollout check that if packaging or runtime flags changed, pipeline fails unless cache-namespace is bumped.

Anna (Eng-SRE): For the incident record: root cause = shared KV/prefix cache between rollouts due to missing namespace versioning in r2025-03-01 packaging; impact = stale/mismatched assistant outputs for 3 customers; mitigation = rollback traffic + per-tenant cache invalidation + short-term TTL; plan = enforce namespace per-rollout + rekey migration + automated pipeline guard.

Jordan (Support): Thanks team — I'll close the customer escalations once I get thumbs up from AcmePay. Please ping here when the PRs merge and when deploys include the cache-namespace change.

Sam (Eng-ML): Noted. PRs: #4827 (runtime: namespace headers), #4828 (pipeline: cache-namespace guard). I'll ping when merged.

DeployBot: rollback r2025-03-01-14 -> r2025-02-27-09 completed at 2025-03-02T02:28Z.

Jordan (Support): Closing loop: AcmePay confirmed fix, Tutorly gating tests passed. Marking this resolved for now; will follow up after the namespace change lands.
